verdict.rationale: Sill notices when it is holding frames back, warns over the picture, and offers a quality the link can carry. It also starts remote sessions at a lower quality and lets the user pick a Quality level on the device or Mac. However, the adaptation is a prompt the user must act on rather than automatic adjustment, and the manual control is a single Quality setting rather than separate resolution and frame-rate controls. missing for 10: fully automatic mid-session quality adaptation, explicit user-set resolution and frame-rate controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power user, quality adapts when the link falls behind, and I can set resolution and frame rate myself

citations.quote: Sill for Mac notices that it is holding frames back and tells your device, which says so over the picture and, in its Settings, offers a quality the link can carry.
Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry
Pick a lower Quality in the settings panel on your iPhone or iPad, or in the Sill menu on your Mac.
